newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM Meciar rebuffs European parliament.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM Meciar rebuffs European parliament.

text.p: Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar hit back at the European parliament on Monday for its criticism of his country's slow moves towards democracy.
Last week Herbert Boesch, co-chairman of a joint committee of the European and Slovak parliaments, warned that Slovakia was in danger of missing the boat for integration into the European Union.
But in an interview with the official TASR news agency, Meciar said the European parliament had over-stepped itself.
"We are a sovereign state and nobody can give us any ultimatums let alone a group of members of the European Parliament which has no decision-making authority," Meciar said.

At its meeting last week, the joint committee unanimously adopted three recommendations -- to be fulfilled by the end of November -- aimed at improving Slovakia's image in its efforts to be in on the next wave of EU expansion.

They called for the revival of dialogue between the ruling coalition and the opposition and between the government and the president and for enabling opposition parties to sit on parliamentary committees overseeing the secret service and military intelligence.
It also called for a law on the use of minority languages in official communications.
The three matters have been the subject of previous concerns raised by the European Parliament, warnings which have been largely ignored by the ruling coalition.

Slovakia also wants to be among the first new members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) but its chances have virtually vanished after repeated western criticism of the pace of democratic reform.
